summary: ASTRO is an interactive 3D game for young people that brings NASA's retired machines on the Moon and Mars back to life. NASA has left hundreds of objects on these worlds, and each one has a story. ASTRO turns every abandoned vehicle into a playable mission: players go through its real stages, from landing and driving to discoveries and its final resting place, and complete challenges about what it did and what it taught us. Our first level is the Mars twins, Spirit and Opportunity. Opportunity was planned to last 90 days and ran for almost 15 years. By turning "space junk" into stories people can play, ASTRO helps the next generation see these machines as milestones of discovery. Next we plan a classroom mode for schools and a VR version.
details:
ASTRO is a 3D, game-based storytelling experience that brings NASA's retired vehicles on the Moon and Mars back to life. Each abandoned vehicle becomes a playable mission. Our first level tells the story of the Mars Exploration Rover twins, Spirit and Opportunity. They were built for 90 days: Spirit worked for over six years and Opportunity for almost fifteen.

How it works: Players start from a 3D solar system, travel to Mars, accept the mission and hear a narrated briefing on a 3D globe showing the real landing sites (Gusev Crater and Meridiani Planum). They meet the rover and its six real science instruments (Pancam, Mini-TES, Microscopic Imager, APXS, Mössbauer and the Rock Abrasion Tool), each with a hands-on "Try It!" simulation. Then they prepare the rover, fix a system fault, and watch one continuous 3D launch-and-landing sequence from Earth to the Martian surface. Captain Saqr, an original cartoon astronaut, guides players with voice and subtitles. Players earn points, badges and collectible robot cards. Collecting all 10 cards unlocks "Create Your Own Mission".

Benefits and impact: ASTRO turns "space junk" into heritage. It makes NASA mission history fun for young people, builds curiosity about space science, and teaches by doing, not only reading. Research supports this: serious games beat conventional teaching for learning and for remembering it later (Wouters et al., 2013).

Creativity: ASTRO is built as a reusable mission engine. Every vehicle follows the same stages, so new levels (Lunar Roving Vehicles, Sojourner, Viking, Ingenuity) can be added easily.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js (3D graphics), Web Audio API (music and sound effects), Web Speech API (narration), GitHub and GitHub Pages. The whole game is one self-contained file that runs in any browser on phones, tablets and computers, with no install. Claude (Anthropic) was used as an AI coding assistant.

Factors we considered: scientific accuracy (facts checked against NASA sources), accessibility (captions, adjustable voice speed, works on any device), and scalability. Next steps: a classroom mode for schools, a VR version, and new levels for the Moon.
